findings.statement: lowers risk when age is low for the heart rate; reversible defect raises risk through it from about 1% to 4%
findings.check: probe age x thal and thalach x thal
findings.evidence: normal scan: contribution -1.76 at 35, -0.33 at 50, 0 from 54 (boundary age - 0.28*152.5 = 10.9 gives 53.6); higher thalach makes it more negative (-0.21 at 130 -> -1.80 at 190); with a reversible defect it is 0 everywhere
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --sweep age=35,42,45,50,54,56,60,66,72 --sweep thal=3,7
uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --set age=45 --sweep thalach=100,118,130,140,150,160,165,175,190 --sweep thal=3,7

findings.statement: 80 of 242 on, 11% vs 60% disease
findings.evidence: 80 rows (33.1%), outcome 11.2% where it acts vs 60.5% elsewhere
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify ablate experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --part ann_31 --to zero

findings.statement: for patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan, age rises in a jump (typical patient from about 12% at 42 to about 28% at 66)
findings.check: probe age sweep with thal=7 (typical patient)
findings.evidence: with a reversible defect the gate is off at every age for the typical patient (risk flat at 41.9%, contribution 0); only 3 of 90 such patients have the gate on (subgroup thal==7). The 12%->28% numbers belong to the normal-scan case; the jump applies to a small minority (14% of moving curves)
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --sweep age=35,42,45,50,54,56,60,66,72 --sweep thal=3,7
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --where "thal == '7'"

findings.statement: active 33.1%; 50.7% of 152 without defect vs 3.3% of 90 with; AUC 0.9434->0.9378
findings.evidence: 3 of 90 active (3.3%), 50.7% in the rest; AUC 0.9378
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --where "thal == '7'"

commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --sweep oldpeak=0,0.5,0.75,0.8,1.0,1.4,1.7,2.0,2.8,4 --sweep slope=1,2

uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --where "oldpeak > 1.66"

findings.statement: raises risk mainly with a flat ST segment, ST depression counts more for them
findings.check: probe oldpeak x slope; subgroup slope==2
findings.evidence: flat: contribution +0.09 at 0 mm to +0.68 at 4 mm; upsloping: 0 until 4 mm (+0.16); active in 98.2% of 110 flat-slope patients vs 6.8% of others
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --sweep oldpeak=0,0.5,0.75,0.8,1.0,1.4,1.7,2.0,2.8,4 --sweep slope=1,2
uv run python -m explaneat verify subgroup experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --where "slope == '2'"

findings.statement: not-flat patients switch on when oldpeak - 0.012 chol > 0.03 (chol 186-417)
findings.evidence: off at 2.8 mm, on at 4.0 mm (boundary 0.03 + 0.012*240 = 2.9 mm)
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-2103cc --sweep oldpeak=0,0.5,0.75,0.8,1.0,1.4,1.7,2.0,2.8,4 --sweep slope=1,2

findings.statement: fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers risk
findings.evidence: raised blood sugar is a known risk factor; the model gives the opposite sign

findings.statement: typical angina gets the lowest risk, below no-symptom patients
findings.evidence: asymptomatic patients in this dataset are known to carry high disease rates, so this is plausible for the data but counter-intuitive clinically

findings.statement: fixed thallium defect lowers risk (n=15)
findings.evidence: a fixed defect is usually a sign of past infarction; small group

findings.statement: higher cholesterol lowers risk through this part
findings.evidence: counter-directional inside the part; offset by cholesterol's direct positive edge
